name: Angle-resolved Shubnikov-de Haas and cantilever dHvA quantum oscillations of PdGa, 1.5-30 K up to 18 T
plain_name: Map a metal's electron orbits from resistance wiggles in an 18 T magnet
description: Record transverse magnetoresistance (4 mA rms, 22.08 Hz lock-in, Al wire bonds) and capacitive cantilever torque of a 4 x 1 x 0.2 mm3 PdGa platelet at constant temperatures 1.5-30 K in a helium-flow cryostat in fields up to 18 T, rotating the sample in 4 degree steps over 90 degrees; extend to 0.1 K in a dilution refrigerator.
keywords: Map a metal's electron orbits from resistance wiggles in an 18 T magnet

sources.citation: N. Huber, I. Volkau, A. Engelhardt, I. Sheikin, A. Bauer, C. Pfleiderer, M.A. Wilde, 'Fermi surface and magnetic breakdown in PdGa', arXiv:2504.12379 (2025)

reported_equipment: cantilever-based torque magnetometer with capacitive readout

requirements.rationale: Both SdH and dHvA data were recorded up to 18 T.
Effective masses come from constant-temperature data between 1.5 and 30 K.
AC magnetoresistance requires wired sample contacts.
The 4 mm x 1 mm platelet footprint has a circumscribed diameter of 4.13 mm (sqrt(17) = 4.123 mm, rounded up).
Optional: the excitation current was 4 mA rms.
Optional extension: additional SdH measurements down to 0.1 K in a dilution refrigerator.
Optional: the source used a helium-flow cryostat; any machine reaching 1.5 K at 18 T would serve.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
